pages.text: $(bold)Bendable, Not Breakable$()$(br2)The tier system is designed to be bent by skilled players, not broken. A shortcut that gets you one next-tier item early is a feature. A shortcut that skips an entire tier is a bug.$(br2)$(bold)Break$() = Create mixing produces diamonds in $(t1)Tier 1$().$(br)$(bold)Bend$() = Create mixing produces steel from iron+coal at a worse ratio than Thermal.

$(bold)Abundance, Not Scarcity$()$(br2)There are no resource locks. Crops, building mods, QoL features, and travel are available from day one. What is gated is $(italic)power$() — weapons, armor, magic systems, and dimensions.$(br2)You should never feel blocked from having fun. You may feel blocked from the next tier of power. That is intentional.

$(bold)Death Is a Cost$()$(br2)Keep inventory is on. You will never lose your items on death. However, your equipped gear loses durability — and at zero durability, items go $(italic)inert$(): they stop working but remain in your inventory.$(br2)Dying in $(t1)Tier 1$() is cheap. Dying in the End with $(t4)Tier 4$() gear is genuinely expensive. $(thing)Soulbound$() enchantment is the ultimate insurance.$(br2)See $(l:icraft:systems/death_penalty)Death Penalty$(/l) for full details.

$(bold)Boss Fights Are the Pinnacle$()$(br2)The best weapons in the pack — $(thing)Simply Swords$() unique weapons — drop only from bosses. They cannot be crafted. They cannot be traded for. Each is thematically matched to its source boss.$(br2)This means engaging with the combat system isn't just fun — it's the only path to the best gear. Tier skipping via crafting will never give you what a boss kill will.
